task: Fix the slow query plan regression after statistics were not collected on the new partition.

candidate_memories.content: Query optimizer uses a full table scan on the new November partition because no statistics exist for that partition.
Run ANALYZE on the November partition to generate statistics; the query planner will then use the correct index scan.
Partitioned tables require ANALYZE to be run explicitly on each new partition; autovacuum does not cover new partitions.
When adding a new table partition, include ANALYZE in the post-partition-creation runbook.
Only queries that filter on the November partition date range are affected; other partitions have correct statistics.
The transactions table is partitioned by month; each partition is created on the first of the month.
Session 4 note: the DBA team increased the default statistics target from 100 to 300 for the transactions table.
Old practice: ANALYZE was run manually on the whole table before partitioning was introduced.
PostgreSQL autovacuum runs on the parent table but does not automatically trigger on child partitions.
Session 11 note: a query performance review showed all other partitions have query plans with index scans.
Old partition guide: partition creation was a manual DBA step before it was automated in the pipeline.
New table partitions require explicit statistics collection before the query planner can generate optimal plans.
Session 8 note: the analytics team added a new dashboard for partition-level query latency.
The transactions table has 900 million rows across 18 partitions.
A query plan review in session 6 confirmed the October partition uses an efficient index scan.
Partition creation is automated via a cron job that runs on the 28th of each month.
Partitioned tables should have a post-creation automation hook that runs ANALYZE on each new partition.
Session 3 note: the DBA team added partition pruning hints to the most frequent reporting queries.
Old statistics guide: the statistics target for the transactions table was 100 before the DBA review.
The reporting dashboard queries are run against a read replica that has a 5-minute replication lag.
